mismatches.findings: MISMATCH (snapshot) — category (b), false positive. Two compounding probe defects: (1) Stale path / move not followed — the file was created@891 at RevEng/jfred-unified-load.js, later worked on as RevEng/unified/jfred-unified-load.js, and now lives on disk at RevEng/unified/jfred-unified-load.js. The probe keyed on the first-seen path (buildFilePathIndex) which is not on disk, so it fell through to the snapshot reference instead of comparing against the real current file. (2) Snapshot-predates-final-edit — trySnapshotVerify replays ALL 25 edits (final state) but compares against the LAST file-history-snapshot at line 1774, and there is exactly 1 edit AFTER that snapshot (edit@1780). So the snapshot is one edit stale; a correct full replay necessarily differs from it ⇒ false MISMATCH. The replay engine is correct; the probe's reference is wrong.

relevantPipelineSourceFiles.relevance: trySnapshotVerify() compares the full-replay (all edits) against the LAST snapshot, which is stale whenever any edit follows the last snapshot — exactly this case.
findLastSnapshotContent() supplies the line-1774 snapshot that predates edit@1780, the root of the false diff.
verifyTarget() only checks fs.existsSync(fullPath) at the stale recorded path; it never relocates to the current unified/ path via cp/mv lineage, forcing the snapshot fallback.

mismatches.findings: MISMATCH (on-disk) — category (b), basename-collision bug. Within session 3b6806e4 the basename 'launch.json' was recorded at THREE distinct paths: src/.vscode/launch.json, RevEng/.claude/launch.json, and src/.claude/launch.json (all confirmed: the latter two exist on disk; the probe's chosen fullPath src/.vscode/launch.json is missing, but a sibling .vscode copy exists one level up). The probe keys targets by basename (collectProbeTargets / buildFilePathIndex), so edits to three different files are merged into a single replay stream and then compared to one on-disk file. The 4 'ignored' edits are the tell — edits to the other two launch.json files that don't belong to the compared file. The mismatch is an artifact of conflating distinct files by basename, not a replay error.
